name: Auth pages
author: Anvil contributors
description: Checks that the login, signup and password-reset pages load with the right fields, that sign-in forms cannot put the password in the URL, and walks you through rate limiting, reset links and logout by hand.

checks.title: Login page at /login does not load with a password field
checks.why: People who come back to your app go to /login first. If it is missing, errors, or has no password field, they cannot get in. If your app signs in somewhere else (for example /signin or only with Google), ignore this.
checks.fix: Make /login (or a redirect from it) show the sign-in form, and check it loads without errors when signed out.

checks.title: Signup page at /signup does not load with a password field
checks.why: New users need to be able to create an account. A broken signup page loses every new visitor. If your app uses another URL (for example /register) or passwordless sign-up, ignore this.
checks.fix: Make /signup (or a redirect from it) show the sign-up form, and check it loads without errors when signed out.

checks.title: Password reset page at /forgot-password does not load
checks.why: Users who forget their password need a way back in; without one they leave or email you. If your reset page lives at another URL, ignore this and answer the reset-link human check.
checks.fix: Add a forgot-password page that asks for an email address and sends a one-time reset link.

checks.title: Login form could send the password in the URL
checks.why: A form with a password field and no method="post" is submitted as GET when JavaScript is slow, fails, or the handler forgets preventDefault. The password then lands in the address bar, browser history and server logs.
checks.fix: Add method="post" to the form (keep your JavaScript handler), so a native submit never puts the password in the URL.

checks.title: Signup form could send the password in the URL
checks.why: Same as the login form: without method="post", a native submit puts the new password in the URL, history and logs.
checks.fix: Add method="post" to the signup form.

checks.title: Password field has no autocomplete hint
checks.why: Without autocomplete="current-password", password managers fill and save less reliably, which nudges people towards weak, reused passwords.
checks.fix: Add autocomplete="current-password" on the login password field and autocomplete="new-password" on signup and reset.

humanChecks.prompt: After 10 wrong passwords in a row, does the app slow you down, lock the account or ask for a captcha?
steps: Open the login page for an account you own
Enter a wrong password 10 times in a row, quickly
Answer Works if you are slowed down, locked out for a while, or shown a captcha
Answer Broken if every attempt is accepted instantly with no limit

humanChecks.prompt: Does a password-reset link work only once and expire?
steps: Request a password reset for an account you own
Use the link from the email to set a new password
Answer Broken if it lets you set the password a second time

humanChecks.prompt: Do login and reset give the same message for an email that has no account?
steps: On the reset page, enter an email that has an account, then one that does not
On the login page, try a wrong password for a real account, then any password for a made-up email
Answer Broken if the messages tell you which emails have accounts

humanChecks.prompt: After logging out, are private pages really closed?
steps: Sign in and open a private page (dashboard, settings)
Press the browser Back button, then reload the page
Answer Broken if the private page still shows your data after the reload
